review_scope: Independent review of the first frozen R9 identity/site candidate; no implementation edits

finding.problem: The new site support predicate accepts same_physical_site as field-level equivalence. The existing helper's address regex can match only the street when city/state lack commas. It therefore treats '100 Main Street Austin TX' and '100 Main Street Dallas TX' as equivalent, allowing a current Dallas claim to attest a stored Austin site or suppress a site conflict.
finding.deterministic_proof: With backend src on PYTHONPATH, same_physical_site('100 Main Street Austin TX', '100 Main Street Dallas TX') returned True. The project-state code passes this result directly into site support and claim equivalence.
finding.required_repair: Keep the R9 field-specific current-admitted-claim design. Narrow site projection equivalence so same street with contradictory city/state cannot support the stored value or collapse competing claims. Add a project-state regression for distinct cities with the same street and preserve valid formatting-only equivalence. Do not broaden global matching architecture.

gate_state: The controller reported fresh 19/19 deterministic gates passed on this candidate, but they do not cover the demonstrated site counterexample. This candidate is not independently accepted.
